correctness.rationale: For each generic plane, each intersected antipodal facet pair contributes exactly two section sides; the six square and eight hexagonal facets yield N=4+2[2z>y]+2[2y<x]+2[2z<x] for ordered absolute normal coordinates x>y>z>0. This partitions the 48-fold fundamental normal chamber into explicit spherical triangles and a triangulated quadrilateral with disjoint interiors. The standard positive-denominator solid-angle identity evaluates their areas; normalization gives the three probabilities, all strictly positive and summing to one. Separately 36 edges each connect vertex vectors of cosine 4/5, giving E N = 36 arccos(4/5)/pi and agreeing with the distribution. The standalone stdlib program confirms 24 vertices, 36 edges, exact rational-normal examples and independent quadrature/Haar simulations, which corroborate but do not replace the continuum proof.

value.rationale: The regular truncated octahedron is a canonical Archimedean solid and three-dimensional lattice Voronoi cell; central random-section polygon type is a natural geometric-probability invariant. Its 6/8/10 type law gives the exact occurrence probability of each distinct topology, which cannot be recovered from a mean vertex count alone. The normal-cone decomposition supplies a conceptual explanation and a reproducible exact elementary distribution rather than an arbitrary computational slice. This improves the available description of planar section complexity of that natural body.
